messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: high-severity - KV cache fragmentation + continuous-batching growth detected on prod cluster 'gpu-pool-3' (svc=inference). Observed: rapid VRAM consumption, cuda OOMs, and increased p99 latency. Paging eng-oncall. thread_ts=2147623456
cheng-wu: seeing it in metrics too. KV cache live size jumped ~3x over last 8m. p50 token latency up ~150ms, p99 spiking to 1.2s. CUDA OOM logs show pytorch::cudaMalloc failing during batch allocation. :eyes:
maria-gonzalez: confirmed customer-facing errors for a few tenants, 503s from gateway. Which deploys occurred in the last hour?
noah-k: rolled continuous-batching tweak 59m ago — changed max_batch_age_ms from 8 -> 25 and enabled aggressive prefix caching. I have the rollout window.
sophie-lee: that config was targeted at small-latency workloads, but I flagged increased cache retention risk. Might be related.
achj: (typing) @aj FYI, can you look at arena metrics and fragmentation counters?
aj: on it. pulling `gpu-pool-3` allocator histograms now. initial glance: slab occupancy highly uneven, free-slab fragmentation high. Suspect slab-size mismatch + longer-lived Kv entries.
ops-oncall: customers impacted: 3 high-traffic tenants with inference queues backing up, support tickets opened. CS alerted. Estimating severity: Sev2.
cheng-wu: reproducing locally with the same max_batch_age_ms shows lots of small KV entries that don't coalesce; continuous batching is creating many short-lived cache keys, then retention keeps them longer, preventing reuse and causing fragmentation.
maria-gonzalez: mitigation options? rollback config, force an arena compaction, or patch allocator to coalesce small slabs. Which is fastest?
noah-k: fastest is rollback the batch_age change. That will reduce short-lived KV creation immediately. Second is a hotpatch to trigger compaction in the arena, but that's riskier.
sophie-lee: can we do a targeted rollback on gpu-pool-3 only? We still want the change in other pools.
aj: yes, config is per-pool via remote-feature flags. I can flip it in ~2 min.
cheng-wu: while we do that, I can push a compaction job to reclaim free ranges (non-disruptive) — it runs as a GC and throttles itself. Command: ```sh
# run arena compaction (safe, throttled)
redwood-cli admin arena compact --pool gpu-pool-3 --throttle 0.2
```
ops-oncall: run rollback first so customer errors stop ASAP. compaction can run after rollback to stabilize memory.
noah-k: rolling back batch_age change on gpu-pool-3 now. Command: `redwood-cli config set --pool gpu-pool-3 continuous-batching.max_batch_age_ms=8 --source rollback`
deploy-bot: Deploy job started: rollback-config/gpu-pool-3 @noah-k (job id d9f4). Promoting to 4 clusters.
(2m) noah-k: rollback applied to 4/4 nodes in pool. traffic metrics should start normalizing in ~30-60s.
(45s) ops-oncall: p99 latency dropping, token throughput stabilizing. OOM logs have stopped. :thumbsup:
maria-gonzalez: customer impact update: CS confirms error rate down to baseline for 3 tenants. closing active Sev2 alerts for those customers but keep incident open until fragmentation counters decrease.
achj: starting arena compaction now with the command Cheng posted. Monitor compaction progress: `redwood-cli admin arena status --pool gpu-pool-3`
cheng-wu: compaction reported 38% reclaimed over 15min, fragmentation metric (slab_free_ratio) trending down. Good.
sophie-lee: what's root cause summary we can put on postmortem? I propose: continuous-batching config increased batch age -> higher number of short-lived KV keys + aggressive prefix caching -> slabs sized suboptimally for new access patterns -> allocator fragmentation + intermittent cudaMalloc failures.
aj: agree. Also mention lack of canary traffic profile mismatch (we tested with low prefix churn). We'll add action items: 1) refine canary to include prefix-heavy workloads; 2) add automated guardrail that prevents max_batch_age_ms > 15 for pools with older slab layout; 3) implement on-the-fly slab coalescing path in allocator.
ops-oncall: handoff: I'll stay as incident lead for next 2 hours while compaction finishes and telemetry stabilizes. If anyone else needs to be looped in (eng-sre, security), ping now.
cheng-wu: collecting logs for postmortem: allocator histograms, pytorch cudaMalloc traces, and config rollout history. Dumping to /tmp/2147623456-collector.tar.gz and uploading to the incident runbook.
maria-gonzalez: thanks all. small follow-up: can we add customer-facing note template for CS? draft: "We identified a transient memory fragmentation issue in our inference pool that caused elevated latencies and occasional request failures. We rolled back a recent batching config and ran compaction; service is restored. We're performing a full post-incident review."
noah-k: ok to close paging after compaction completes and fragmentation metric < 10% for 30m. ops-oncall will close.
incident-bot: Incident actions logged. Attachments: rollback job d9f4, compaction job c4a1, diagnostic bundle /tmp/2147623456-collector.tar.gz.
ops-oncall: compaction completed. slab_free_ratio = 8.9% and p99 latency steady. I'm closing the incident in 30m if stable. Thanks team. :handshake:
